chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Jimmie Lunceford's band in the Labor Day parade
summary: Howard recalls Lunceford's band representing Local 767 in a Labor Day parade and the union marching band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I think there's a mention here in the article about -- mentioned some pictures you have. It mentioned
something about Jimmie Lunceford's band in a union parade or something?
Yeah.
Would you tell us about that?
Yeah, I can tell you about that.
What happened?
Nothing. Just come down and played the parade, that's all. Just played.
It was a union parade.
Yes.
Was that a Labor Day parade?
Labor Day, yes, a Labor Day parade.
And Jimmie Lunceford's band played in it. What, representing Local 767, or --
Yeah. Representing Local 767, and I got the picture of him out there doing it, too.
Were there any other bands involved?
No, just Jimmie Lunceford.
I heard -- I think Marshall Royal told me that one time 767 had a marching band that would march once a year in the Labor Day parade. Is that right?
Yes, they did have. Now, I can't remember what that was. You'll have to forgive me. There are some things you can't remember.
Yeah.
I can't remember that, but I know they did have a band (unintelligible),
And Marshall didn't know of any time that they would march except that once a year.
That once a year.
I wondered if you knew of any other activities like that.
No. Marshall would know about it because he was in it.
I think he said he was.
Yeah, he was in it. I can't remember too much about it. You know, it's kind of hard to keep up with bands.
Yeah.

Yeah, there's a lot of them, and a whole lot of people running them, too. I didn't get a chance to do anything with them. Can you think of anything else on there that might -- that I could comment on or anything?
